note: Authored pack: s27 (Interview Mastery) theory+interview, s28 (Coding Patterns/Final Practice) coding+logic+checkpoint, s29 (Resume Project Labs) solved+debug+defense — 20 each.

items.q: Interview ka pehla 2 minute kya decide karta hai?
items.a: Problem understanding aur approach clarity. Interviewer dekhta hai: sawal ko clarify kiya? constraints poocha? brute force → better approach ka journey dikhaya? Isliye pehle clarifying questions, phir approach, phir code.

items.q: AI Engineer vs Data Scientist vs ML Engineer — role boundaries batao.
items.a: DS: analysis, experiments, statistics aur business insights. MLE: production systems, deployment, infra, reliability. AI Engineer: LLM/RAG/agent systems, prompt/eval design aur product integration. Overlap zyada hai — job description padho.

items.q: Interview me STAR method kab aur kaise use karte hain?
items.a: Behavioural questions ke liye: Situation, Task, Action, Result — aur Result me number (latency kam hui, revenue impact, time saved). 60-90 second me ek story, technical depth optional follow-up ke liye rakho.

items.q: 'Tell me about yourself' ka structured jawab kya hoga?
items.a: 3 parts: ab kya karte ho (current focus), relevant experience ka 1-2 proof point (project + number), aur is role me kyun (specific). 90 second max, resume padhna nahi hai.

items.q: Interview me 'I don't know' kaise bolna chahiye?
items.a: Honestly bolo, phir reasoning dikhao: 'mujhe exact nahi pata, par main aise approach karta — X documentation dekhunga, Y experiment karunga'. Guess ko fact ki tarah mat bolo.

items.q: Interview me trade-off bhasha kyun zaroori hai?
items.a: Seniority ka signal: 'simple option X, scalable option Y, main Y chununga kyunki data size Z hai' — choice + reason + cost. Sirf 'best practice' bolna weak lagta hai.

items.q: Coding interview me pehle brute force likhna chahiye ya optimal?
items.a: Brute force bolo aur uski complexity batao, phir bottleneck identify karke optimize karo — interviewer ko thinking process dikhta hai. Direct optimal likhna theek hai agar approach pehle verbalize kar do.

items.q: Interview me complexity bataate waqt kaunsi galtiyan hoti hain?
items.a: Average vs worst case mix karna, hidden costs ignore karna (string concat, sort in loop, dict hashing), aur space complexity bhoolna (recursion stack). Har loop/recursion par explicitly bolo.

items.q: ML interview me 'metric kyun chuna' ka jawab kaise dete hain?
items.a: Business cost se: false negative mehnga tha → recall-first, aur class imbalance tha → PR-AUC. Phir threshold cost matrix se set kiya. Metric justification mehngi hoti hai sirf accuracy batane se.

items.q: System design interview me pehle kya karte ho?
items.a: Requirements clarify (functional + non-functional: latency, scale, consistency, budget), rough numbers (QPS, data size), phir high-level boxes, phir deep dive on the critical path. Perfect design nahi, structured reasoning.

items.q: Interview me project explain karne ka best structure kya hai?
items.a: Problem + constraint → approach (aur kya options the) → implementation highlights → measured result → what you'd change now. Numbers aur trade-offs se credibility aati hai.

items.q: Resume me project bullet kaise likhna chahiye?
items.a: Action + technology + measurable outcome: 'Built RAG service over 12k docs with hybrid retrieval; cut support answer time 35% and p95 latency to 400ms'. Ownership verb se shuru karo, responsibility nahi outcome likho.

items.q: Interview me gap ya career switch kaise explain karte hain?
items.a: Short, factual, forward-looking: kya kiya us samay (skills, projects, certifications), kya seekha, aur ab role ke liye kyun ready ho. Defensive tone nahi, blame nahi.

items.q: Interview me salary discussion ka approach kya hoga?
items.a: Research se range pata karo, ek number ki jagah range + 'role ke scope par depend' bolo, aur total package (bonus, equity, learning) dekho. Pehle apni value ka proof do, phir numbers.

items.q: Interview me 'do you have questions for us' — kya poochhna chahiye?
items.a: Team ka current biggest challenge, success ka definition 6 mahine me, architecture/data stack, on-call aur review culture, aur next steps. Ye poochhna engagement aur seriousness dikhata hai.
items.x: Work aur team ke baare me poochho.

items.q: Mock interview ka practice loop kaise banate ho?
items.a: Timer ke saath bolkar practice (loud), recording suno, feedback rubric (structure/clarity/depth), aur weak areas par targeted drill. Har week 2 mock — generic reading se improvement nahi hoti.

items.q: Interview me whiteboard/coding task me testing kaise dikhate ho?
items.a: Solution likhne ke baad khud edge cases bolo aur test karo: empty input, single element, duplicates, negative/zero, large input. Interviewer ke poochne se pehle karna strong signal hai.

items.q: Interview me production experience kaise prove karte ho?
items.a: Concrete incidents aur numbers: 'rollback 5 min me kiya', 'alert se detect hua', 'p95 900ms se 180ms', 'migration expand-contract se zero downtime'. Stories + metrics > buzzwords.

items.q: Interview me team conflict ka jawab kaise dena chahiye?
items.a: Non-blaming, process-focused: disagreement kya thi, data kisne diya, kaise decide hua (experiment/review), aur relationship kaise maintain hui. Empathy + decisiveness dikhao.

items.q: Final round ke baad follow-up ka kya protocol?
items.a: 24 ghante me short thank-you note with one concrete value point ya question ka answer, aur timeline poochho. Zyada follow-up (har din ping) unprofessional lagta hai.

items.q: Interview: 'Tumhara sabse challenging project kaunsa tha?' — 90 second answer structure do.
items.a: Context (problem + constraint) → mera role aur trade-offs → kya technically hard tha → measured outcome → ab kya better karta. Example: RAG service, table-heavy PDFs par recall low tha, routing + table-aware chunking se 0.6 → 0.86.

items.q: Interview: 'Ek technical failure batao' — jawab kaise banao ge?
items.a: Failure + iska asar + maine kya diagnose kiya + fix + system/process me kya permanent badla. Example: status filter missing se dashboard metric 20% inflated tha → filter fix + regression test + definition doc.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapne kis cheez ko simplify kiya aur kyun?'
items.a: Over-engineered multi-agent setup ko single agent + deterministic state machine me convert kiya kyunki task me single owner tha — result: 40% cost kam, debugging aasan, reliability 3% upar. Simplicity ko result ke saath justify karo.

items.q: Interview: 'Aap decision kaise lete ho jab data adhoora ho?'
items.a: Data jo hai usse baseline banao, reversible option chuno (feature flag/canary), timebox experiment chalao, aur assumption explicitly likho. Data complete hone ka wait mat karo, par andaze ko fact bhi mat banao.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapko code review me kya sabse pehle dikhta hai?'
items.a: Correctness edge cases, error handling, aur tests; phir naming/readability; performance last (aur only if hot path ho). Review comment me reason aur alternative deta hoon, style nit ko blocking nahi banata.

items.q: Interview: 'Data quality issue mila to aap kya karte ho?'
items.a: Quantify (kitne rows/kaunse segments), root cause (upstream change/join/parse), mitigate (filter + report), phir permanent fix (contract + assertion + alert) aur stakeholder ko numbers ke saath update.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapne kisi model ko reject kyun kiya jiska offline score accha tha?'
items.a: Latency/cost budget se bahar tha aur interpretability requirement fail karta tha — offline F1 2 point zyada thi par p95 900ms. Simpler model chuna aur threshold tune kiya, production me bhi behtar perform kiya.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapke liye good code kya hai?'
items.a: Correct (edge cases handled), readable (names + structure), testable (pure functions, injected deps), observable (logs/metrics), aur boring (no clever tricks). Teen criteria bolkar ek example do.

items.q: Interview: 'Production me tumhara sabse bada incident?'
items.a: Report query ne primary DB ke connection pool exhaust kar diya → mitigation: query limit + read replica; permanent: nightly pre-aggregation, statement timeouts, alert on pool wait. Timeline aur MTTR numbers ke saath bolo.

items.q: Interview: 'Legacy code me change kaise karte ho jahan tests nahi hain?'
items.a: Characterization tests pehle (current behaviour document karo), phir chhote refactor steps with green tests, seam introduce karo (dependency inject) aur risky path ko feature flag ke peeche rakho.

items.q: Interview: 'Aap estimation kaise karte ho?'
items.a: Work ko chhote pieces me todo, unknowns identify karo, aur range do ('2-4 din, agar X API aisa behave kare to 1 din'). Happens events ke baad estimate update karo — ek number pakad kar rakhna unprofessional hai.

items.q: Interview: 'Aap prioritization kaise karte ho jab sab kuch urgent ho?'
items.a: Impact × effort × risk matrix, aur jo irreversible/reputational risk ho use pehle. Sab kuch urgent nahi hota — stakeholder ke saath explicitly trade-off discuss karta hoon aur outcome measure karta hoon.

items.q: Interview: 'Aap feedback kaise lete ho?'
items.a: Curiosity ke saath: specific examples poochho, summarize karke confirm karo, aur ek action lena. Defensiveness se learning band ho jaati hai — 'koi example de sakte ho' powerful question hai.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapki documentation approach kya hai?'
items.a: Design doc me problem/options/decision (ADR style), runbook me exact commands, aur README me setup steps. Docs code ke saath versioned aur PR me update hote hain — wiki drift nahi.

items.q: Interview: 'Aap experimentation (A/B) ke results kaise interpret karte ho?'
items.a: Pre-registered metric + sample size, novelty effect, segmentation, aur guardrail metrics. Statistical significance ke saath practical significance bhi dekho (3% lift chhoti sample par meaningless).

items.q: Interview: 'Aap AI/LLM ke output ko trustworthy kaise banate ho?'
items.a: Grounding (retrieval + citations), abstention threshold, structured output validation, aur eval suite with regression gates. Trust build hota hai verification se, claim se nahi.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapko naya domain 2 hafte me pick karna hai — plan kya hoga?'
items.a: Week 1: docs/papers skim + ek end-to-end tutorial chalao + team se 3 sawal (jahan biggest gotchas hain). Week 2: ek chhota real task deliver karo + runbook/document gaps note karo. Learn by shipping.

items.q: Interview: 'Aapki team ko tumse kya process change mila?'
items.a: Eval harness + regression gate (ML changes ke liye), aur incident runbooks. Result: regressions production me 60% kam, on-call pages actionable. Process change ko outcome se justify karo.

items.q: Interview: 'Mentoring me tum kya karte ho?'
items.a: Pairing sessions, review me explanation (kyun, sirf kya nahi), aur stretch task with safety net. Mentor ka success metric mentee ka independence hai, tumhari dependency nahi.

items.q: Interview: 'Aap ethics/PII ke saath model development kaise karte ho?'
items.a: Data minimization, consent/legal check, PII redaction in logs/prompts, bias evaluation per segment, aur documented limitations. Ye baad me add karne wala feature nahi, design constraint hai.

items.q: Two pointers se sorted array me pair dhoondho jinka sum target ho.
items.x: O(n) — brute force O(n^2) se better.

items.q: String me pehla non-repeating character nikalo.
items.x: Counter O(n) hai, phir pehla unique dhoondho.

items.q: Sliding window se longest substring without repeating characters nikalo.
items.x: Window start update karo, phir length.

items.q: Binary search implement karo (boundary-safe).
items.x: lo <= hi aur mid±1 — infinite loop se bachav.

items.q: Anagram groups banao (list of words se).
Two sorted arrays ka merge karo (naya list).
Array me subarray ka maximum sum nikalo (Kadane).
items.x: Kadane O(n) — reset vs extend ka choice.

items.q: Valid parentheses check karo (stack).
items.x: End me stack khaali hona chahiye.

items.q: Linked list reverse karo (iterative).
items.a:
def reverse(head):
    prev = None
    while head:
        nxt = head.next
        head.next = prev
        prev = head
        head = nxt
    return prev

items.q: Number of islands count karo (grid, DFS).
Level-order traversal (BFS) karo binary tree ka.
items.x: Level size snapshot lo, phir iterate.

items.q: Binary tree ka max depth nikalo (recursive).
All permutations generate karo (backtracking).
items.x: Backtracking: choose → recurse → undo (yahan copy se).

items.q: Top-K frequent elements nikalo (heap ke bajaye counting + sort).
items.x: most_common heap internally use karta hai.

items.q: Edit distance (Levenshtein) DP se nikalo.
Coin change minimum coins nikalo (DP).
items.x: Bottom-up DP, INF se unreachable mark.

items.q: Longest increasing subsequence length nikalo (O(n log n)).
LRU cache implement karo (OrderedDict).
Merge intervals karo (sorted by start).
items.x: Overlap ke liye <= (touching intervals bhi merge).

items.q: String ko integer me convert karo bina int() ke (basic parser).
items.a:
def to_int(s):
    s = s.strip()
    sign = -1 if s[:1] == '-' else 1
    if s[:1] in '+-': s = s[1:]
    num = 0
    for ch in s:
        if not ch.isdigit(): break
        num = num * 10 + (ord(ch) - 48)
    return sign * num

items.q: Interviewer: 'Code O(n^2) hai, optimize karo' — pehla step kya bataoge?
items.a: Bottleneck identify: nested loop me kya dobara compute ho raha hai? Agar lookup/search hai to hash/set O(1) laao, agar sorted property hai to two-pointer/binary search, agar repeated subproblem hai to memoization. Claim + complexity bolo.

items.q: Recursion vs iteration — interview me kab kaunsa bolna chahiye?
items.a: Tree/backtracking me recursion clear hoti hai (par stack depth bolna), performance-critical aur deep sequences me iteration. Dono case: recursion likho, phir bolo ki tail-call/iteration se stack bacha sakte hain.

items.q: Hash map use karte hue worst case O(n) kaise ban jaata hai?
items.a: Adversarial/duplicate keys se collisions badh jaate hain (ya hash function bura ho) — phir lookup O(n) ho jaata hai. Isliye average vs worst case dono bolo aur input distribution mention karo.

items.q: Two-pointer approach kab valid hoti hai?
items.a: Jab monotonic property ho (sorted array, ya window me add/remove se condition monotonic change ho). Bina monotonicity ke pointer move karne ka logic galat ho jaata hai.

items.q: Bit manipulation se XOR trick kahan kaam aati hai?
items.a: Jab pairs/cancellation chahiye: single number in duplicate array (a ^ a = 0), missing number, aur swapping. Restriction 'O(1) space' ho to XOR soco.

items.q: Empty input aur single element par tumhare solution ka behaviour kya hona chahiye?
items.a: Explicitly handle: empty → defined output (0/None/[]), single → base case. Interview me bolkar test karo; bahut se candidates yahi edge case miss karte hain.

items.q: Greedy kab galat hota hai (classic example)?
items.a: Jab local optimal global optimal nahi deta — jaise coin change with coins {1,3,4}, amount 6: greedy 4+1+1 = 3 coins, optimal 3+3 = 2. Wahan DP chahiye.

items.q: Memoization aur DP me state kaise define karte ho?
items.a: State = woh minimal information jo future decisions ke liye chahiye. Uske baad transition likho (recurrence) aur base case. Galat state = exponential time ya galat answer.

items.q: Sort karke solve karna kab acceptable hai?
items.a: Jab O(n log n) budget ho aur sorted property se solution simple ho jaaye; interview me bolo ki sort ka cost hai aur kya iske bina possible hai (hash/two-pointer).

items.q: Concurrency question: do threads ek counter increment karein — kya hoga?
items.a: Race condition (read-modify-write atomic nahi) — final value kam ho sakti hai. Fix: lock/atomic ops, ya single-threaded event loop. Python me GIL bytecode-level atomicity deta hai par compound ops safe nahi.

items.q: Interviewer poochta hai 'solution ka space kam karo' — options kya honge?
items.a: In-place algorithm, 1D DP (rolling array), two-pointer instead of extra array, aur recursion depth ko iteration se replace. Har option ka correctness impact bolo.

items.q: Amortized complexity ka matlab kya hai (dynamic array push)?
items.a: Average per-operation cost; occasional expensive op (resize O(n)) ko kai saste ops me spread kar dete hain — isliye push amortized O(1) hai par worst case O(n). Interview me dono bolo.

items.q: Stream/online processing me memory constraint ho to approach?
items.a: Ek pass me state maintain karo (running sums, heap top-K, count-min sketch, reservoir sampling) — sab input materialize karne se bachao. Assumption likho ki kya approximate hai.

items.q: Test cases kaise choose karte ho (coding interview me)?
items.a: Small (1-2 elements), typical case, aur edge (empty, duplicates, negative, all same, extreme values). Ye teen bucket bolo aur ek-ek chalao.

items.q: Interviewer solution me bug dikhata hai — kaise respond karoge?
items.a: Acknowledge karo, effect samjho (kaunse input par fail hoga), fix karo aur same test case add karo. Defensive argue karne se better hai calmly trace karna.

items.q: Undirected graph me cycle detect kaise karoge?
items.a: DFS with parent tracking (visited neighbor jo parent nahi hai → cycle) ya DSU me union fail hone par. Directed me 3-color/recursion-stack method chahiye.

items.q: Interview me solution ke baad 'production me kya badloge' poocha jaaye to?
items.a: Input validation, error handling, logging/metrics, streaming for large input, parallelism, tests, aur config. Ye senior signal hai — chhota code se production code tak ka gap dikhao.

items.q: Approximate solution acceptable ho to kya karoge (exact NP-hard)?
items.a: Approach ke saath trade-off bolo: greedy/heuristic with guarantee ya randomization; accuracy vs latency batao aur eval/counterexample se justify karo. Exact solution ka cost bhi mention karo.

items.q: Coding round ke end me invalid input par kya karna chahiye?
items.a: Explicitly bolo: raise/return error with clear message, aur validation boundary par karo; silent default mat rakho. Plus model kotlin-style contract assertions tests me.

items.q: Interview me complexity improve nahi ho rahi — kya strategy bataoge?
items.a: Constraints se hint lo: n = 1e5 → O(n log n), n = 20 → exponential/bitmask, memory tight → streaming. Phir data structure ka choice (heap, monotonic stack, prefix sums) enumerate karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: do-pointer pattern ke do prerequisites likho.
items.a: Sorted order ya monotonic window property, aur pointer movement se condition ka predictably badalna.

items.q: Checkpoint: sliding window ka template (4 lines) likho.
items.a: left = 0; for right in range(n): window add karo; while invalid: window se hatao, left += 1; best update karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: BFS aur DFS ke use-cases alag kaise likho?
items.a: BFS: shortest path (unweighted), level order. DFS: connectivity, topological sort, backtracking, cycle detection. Dono O(V+E).

items.q: Checkpoint: hash map ke teen use-case likho.
items.a: Frequency count, complement/bool lookup (two-sum), aur grouping by canonical key (anagrams).

items.q: Checkpoint: backtracking ke teen steps likho.
items.a: Choose (path me add) → recurse → unchoose (undo), plus pruning condition.

items.q: Checkpoint: DP likhne ka 4-step process likho.
items.a: State define → recurrence (transition) → base case → answer extraction (aur iteration order).

items.q: Checkpoint: binary search ke do common bugs likho.
items.a: Infinite loop (lo/hi update galat) aur overflow (mid = (lo+hi)//2 Python me safe, C++ me lo + (hi-lo)/2).

items.q: Checkpoint: linked list problems ke teen techniques likho.
items.a: Dummy head (insert/delete simplify), fast-slow pointers (cycle/middle), aur reversal in-place with prev/cur/next.

items.q: Checkpoint: tree traversal ke teen orders aur unka output rule likho.
items.a: Preorder (root, left, right), inorder (left, root, right — BST me sorted), postorder (left, right, root — cleanup/dependency).

items.q: Checkpoint: stack ke teen classic use-case likho.
items.a: Balanced parentheses, monotonic stack (next greater element), aur undo/DFS iterative implementation.

items.q: Checkpoint: heap se do kaam likho.
items.a: Top-K/streaming max-min, aur scheduled work/shortest job first (priority queue). heapq min-heap hai — max ke liye negative values.

items.q: Checkpoint: interval problems ka approach likho (3 steps).
items.a: Start par sort karo, sweep karke overlap/conflict nikalo, aur boundary inclusive/exclusive clearly define karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: matrix problems ke do patterns likho.
items.a: Row/col traversal with direction arrays (BFS/DFS), aur in-place rotation/transpose (index mapping).

items.q: Checkpoint: string building me performance ki teen baatein likho.
items.a: Loop me + se concat O(n^2) ho sakta hai — list + join use karo; sorted/immutable ops copies banate hain; aur slicing O(k).

items.q: Checkpoint: graph representation ke do tarike aur choice?
items.a: Adjacency list (sparse, memory-efficient) vs matrix (dense, O(1) edge lookup). Sparse graphs me list default.

items.q: Checkpoint: recursion ka base case aur progress condition likho.
items.a: Base case termination deta hai aur har call input ko chhota karni chahiye, warna stack overflow/infinite recursion.

items.q: Checkpoint: complexity bataate waqt teen cheezein explicitly bolo.
items.a: Time (worst case), space (extra memory), aur hidden operations (sorting/concat/hash).

items.q: Checkpoint: coding round ka 5-step process likho.
items.a: Clarify constraints → examples banao → brute force + complexity → optimize + verbalize → code → test edge cases.

items.q: Checkpoint: 'divide and conquer' ke do example likho.
items.a: Merge sort (split + merge) aur binary search (half discard); plus quickselect for Kth element.

items.q: Checkpoint: O(1) space optimization ke teen tarike likho.
items.a: In-place swap/reversal, two-pointer/rolling variables, aur input ko hi structure banana (marking via sentinel).

items.q: Real-world: resume project ko 8 hafte me complete karna hai — plan banao.
items.a: Week 1-2: data + baseline + eval (get end-to-end working first). Week 3-5: core feature iterations with metric tracking. Week 6: deploy + monitoring. Week 7: docs + tests + polish. Week 8: interview story (trade-offs + numbers) + demo. Har week ka demo-able output.

items.q: Real-world: project me data nahi hai — synthetic/baseline approach kya hoga?
items.a: Public dataset ya docs se synthetic eval set banao (known gold answers), heuristic baseline banao (rules/TF-IDF), aur data pipeline ko pluggable rakho. Ye approach transparently document karo.

items.q: Real-world: project ko deploy karna hai free tier me — architecture kaise choose karoge?
items.a: Managed services ke free tiers: app container (Render/Fly/Railway), Postgres (Neon/Supabase), object storage (S3/R2), aur scheduled jobs (GitHub Actions). Cold start aur sleep ko document karo, demo ke liye warm-up script rakho.

items.q: Real-world: project me kya dekh ke improve karna hai — measurement plan do.
items.a: Metric define karo (recall@5, p95 latency, cost per task), current value measure karo, ek hypothesis likho, change karo, phir dobara measure. Delta report resume bullet ban jaati hai.

items.q: Real-world: project ka demo video/interview demo ke liye script banao.
items.a: 2 minute: problem (10s), live demo happy path (60s), architecture diagram + ek trade-off (30s), measured result (10s), next step (10s). Live demo fail ho to screenshots fallback rakho.

items.q: Real-world: project me eval suite banao (portfolio ke liye convincing).
items.a: Frozen dataset (JSONL), 3 metrics (quality, latency, cost), automated runner + markdown report, aur CI gate. Interviewer ko ye dikhata hai ki tum measurement culture laate ho, sirf code nahi.

items.q: Real-world: project me observability add karna hai — minimum kya?
items.a: Request logging with request id, latency/error metrics, ek dashboard (transactions/errors/latency), aur ek alert (error rate ya cost). Ye 'toy project' aur 'production-minded' ka farq banata hai.

items.q: Real-world: project ko open source banana hai — repo structure?
items.a: README (problem, demo link, quickstart, architecture, metrics), LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, .env.example, tests, aur CI badge. Screenshots/GIF + setup steps copy-paste-able hone chahiye.

items.q: Real-world: project me testing ka minimum bar kya rakho ge?
items.a: Pure logic ke unit tests, API ke integration tests, aur ek end-to-end smoke test; plus eval regression nightly. Coverage % se zyada 'critical paths covered' matter karta hai.

items.q: Real-world: project me secrets aur .env kaise manage karoge?
items.a: .env locally (gitignored), .env.example versioned with placeholders, aur deploy par platform secrets/env vars. Code me zero hardcoded keys, aur startup validation.

items.q: Real-world: project me time budget khatam ho raha hai — kya pehle finish karoge?
items.a: End-to-end working path (demo), tests for that path, README + metrics, phir polish. Adhoora feature hata do — kam features jo kaam karte hain, zyada features jo tootte hain se behtar.

items.q: Real-world: project par cost cap lagana hai — kya karoge?
items.a: Provider budget alerts, per-request token caps, cache layer, aur ek hard limit (max queries/day) with graceful message. Cost per user metric dashboard par rakho.

items.q: Real-world: project me 'before/after' story banana hai — kaise?
items.a: Baseline (manual process ya simple model) ke metrics capture karo, phir tumhare system ke metrics same dataset par; farq ko % me bolo (latency -60%, cost -40%, accuracy +8pt) aur method document karo.

items.q: Real-world: project me user feedback loop add karna hai (early stage).
items.a: Simple thumbs + optional comment, feedback ko DB me trace id ke saath store, aur weekly review se top issues list. 10 users ka structured feedback > 100 anonymous clicks.

items.q: Real-world: project ke interviews me 'what would you do differently' ka honest material kahan se laoge?
items.a: Decision log maintain karo (ADR: kya chuna, kya option tha, kya result mila). Baad me yehi 'differently' ka evidence banta hai — memory par bharosa nahi karna padta.

items.q: Real-world: project me architecture diagram kaise banao ge (interview-ready)?
items.a: Client → API → services → data stores (arrows par protocol), external deps alag box me, aur legend (sync/async). Hand-drawn simple diagram professional-looking diagram se zyada clear hota hai — ek page par rakho.

items.q: Real-world: project me performance bottleneck mila — portfolio me story kaise banti hai?
items.a: Profile karo (numbers), bottleneck identify karo (line/layer), fix karo, dobara measure karo: 'apply loop 8.2s → vectorized 0.3s'. Ye structure (measure → fix → measure) hi interview me jeetta hai.

items.q: Real-world: project me rollback plan kya hoga (personal project level)?
items.a: Versioned container tags + previous tag par redeploy, DB migrations expand-contract, aur feature flag se naya path off. Personal project me bhi ye habit production interviews me strong signal hai.

items.q: Real-world: project ka 'resume bullet' likho (metric-driven).
items.a: 'Built a hybrid-retrieval RAG assistant over 12k internal docs; improved recall@5 from 0.62 to 0.86 and cut p95 latency to 400ms with reranking + caching.' Format: action + system + metric + lever.

items.q: Real-world: project me code quality bar kaise set karoge (without over-engineering)?
items.a: Linter + formatter, typed public interfaces, tests for critical paths, aur ek ADR per major decision. Baaki polish baad me — working system pehle.

items.q: Project deploy hua par app 500 de raha hai aur logs me kuch nahi. Debug order?
items.a: (1) Health endpoint hit karo, (2) app logs (streaming) check karo — agar khali hain to log level/stdout config issue, (3) env vars missing? (4) start command galat? Structure: pehle availability, phir config, phir code.

items.q: Local me chal raha hai, production me DB connection fail. Kya check karoge?
items.a: Connection string (env var actually set?), DB reachable from prod network (VPC/security group/SSL mode), pool size vs connection limit, aur credentials/rotation. Local vs prod config diff print karo.

items.q: Deployed app pehle request par 30s leta hai, phir fast. Wajah aur fix?
items.a: Cold start (container/sleep) + model/first-call initialization. Fix: warm-up ping (cron/uptime check), lazy init ko startup par move, aur smaller image/deps. UI me loading state honest rakho.

items.q: Project me 'module not found' production me, local me theek. Wajah?
items.a: Dependency lockfile me nahi thi (ya dev-dependency thi) ya case-sensitivity difference (Linux vs Windows paths). Fix: lockfile commit karo, production deps alag rakho, aur import paths exact case me likho.

items.q: CORS error sirf production frontend se, local se nahi. Kya check karoge?
items.a: Allowed origins list me production domain add hai? Wildcard with credentials invalid hota hai, aur preflight OPTIONS allowed hai? Origin exact match karo (scheme + port).

items.q: Scheduled job production me chal hi nahi raha. Debug?
items.a: Timezone (UTC vs local), cron syntax, worker service actually running (logs/heartbeat), aur job queue permissions. Heartbeat metric rakho taaki silent failure na ho.

items.q: Cost alert aaya ki API spend 10x ho gaya. Pehle kya dekhoge?
items.a: Token usage per request (kya prompt/context badha), retry loops, aur naya traffic source. Dashboard se request count + avg tokens pata karo — spike usually prompt size ya retry storm se aata hai.

items.q: Model ne production me bahut galat answer diye, offline eval fine tha. Kya check karoge?
items.a: Train/serve preprocessing mismatch, version mismatch (deployed model vs eval model), aur input distribution shift. Production samples ko capture karke offline replay karo.

items.q: App memory slowly badh rahi hai aur OOM restart hota hai. Approach?
items.a: Memory profile (tracemalloc/psutil) se growth ka site dhoondo, unbounded caches/global lists check karo, aur streaming vs full-load review karo. Restart ke saath heap dump compare karna classic trick hai.

items.q: Git repo me ek build kaam karta hai, doosre machine par nahi. Kya check karoge?
items.a: Lockfile commit, Node/Python version (runtime), env vars, aur OS-specific scripts. Fix: version managers/runtime pinning (nvm, .python-version) aur documented setup steps.

items.q: API timeout ho raha hai sirf peak hours me. Debug plan?
items.a: Percentile latency + pool/queue metrics ko time ke saath correlate karo, DB slow queries aur connection wait time dekho, aur autoscaling rules check karo. Fix: pool tuning + cache + horizontal scale.

items.q: Frontend me API response parse ho raha hai kabhi-kabhi fail. Root cause?
items.a: Response shape mismatch (error case me different schema) ya streaming/partial response. Fix: contract define karo, error shape same rakho, aur client par schema validation (zod/pydantic-like) lagao.

items.q: Password reset email production me nahi aa rahe. Layers kaise check karoge?
items.a: Send API response/logs (provider accepted?), queue/worker running, template/config, aur spam folder. Silent catch ko remove karo — har stage ka log likho.

items.q: Rolling deploy ke baad 5% requests fail ho rahe hain. Hypothesis?
items.a: Mixed versions (old/new) with incompatible API/DB schema — expand-contract migration chahiye. Check: failing requests kis version par gayi (logs me version tag hona chahiye).

items.q: Docker build cache har baar invalidate ho raha hai (slow builds). Fix?
items.a: COPY order theek karo (requirements pehle, code baad me), .dockerignore me node_modules/.git, aur layer me changing files (version stamps) alag rakho. Build time halve ho jaata hai.

items.q: Eval script local par chalta hai, CI me nahi (different numbers). Wajah?
items.a: Random seeds, data version, library versions, ya test order. Fix: seeds pin karo, eval data ko repo/artifact me version karo, aur deterministic ordering.

items.q: Model inference time production me 3x hai local se. Kya check karoge?
items.a: CPU vs GPU, thread/BLAS config, batch size (1 vs batched), quantization/ONNX runtime differences, aur container CPU limits (throttling). cgroup throttling aam wajah hai.

items.q: Project me feature flag add kiya, par flag hamesha default hi le raha hai. Bug?
items.a: Evaluation key missing (user id), SDK cache stale, ya wrong environment/config loaded. Fix: flag evaluation log karo (kaunsa key, kaunsa value) aur default intentionally rakho.

items.q: Production me data pipeline ne kuch rows drop kar diye (silent). Fix kaise permanent karoge?
items.a: Row count assertions per stage (input vs output + expected), drop reasons count karo (null/parse/skip), aur alert on delta. Silent drop sabse khatarnak bug hai — count-based monitoring hi solution hai.

items.q: Local me tests pass hote hain, CI me flaky. Sabse common wajah?
items.a: Time/timezone, shared state between tests, order dependence, network/timeouts, aur unseeded randomness. Fix: fixtures isolate karo, freezegun/frozen time, aur retries nahi — root cause.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare system ka architecture 60 second me explain karo.'
items.a: Client → API (FastAPI, containerized, N replicas) → Postgres (private) + Redis cache; background jobs queue par; retrieval service with vector index; logs/metrics/traces centralized. Deploy CI/CD se, aur ek diagram hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Sabse mushkil technical decision kaunsa tha?'
items.a: Chunking + retrieval strategy (naive fixed-size se recall low tha). Options evaluate kiye (semantic, table-aware, hybrid + RRF), eval set par measure kiya, aur table-aware + hybrid chuna: recall@5 0.62 → 0.86.

items.q: Project defense: 'System kitna scale karega?'
items.a: Currently ~20 rps p95 400ms par single service + shared DB; bottleneck DB connections aur vector index latency hai. Scale plan: read replicas, cache warming, service horizontal scaling, aur index sharding. Numbers + plan.

items.q: Project defense: 'Aapki accuracy ka confidence kya hai — kya dataset chhota nahi tha?'
items.a: Eval set 180 cases (production sampling se), per-bucket breakdown ke saath; confidence interval wide hai small buckets par, isliye wahan 'insufficient data' report karte hain — overclaiming nahi.

items.q: Project defense: 'Kya tumne cost-per-user measure kiya?'
items.a: Haan: ~$0.02 per task (2.4k tokens avg), aur cache hit rate 42% ke saath ~$0.011 effective. Cost dashboard live hai aur budget alert lagaya hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Failure par system ka behaviour kya hai?'
items.a: Degraded modes defined: retrieval down → 'search unavailable' with retry, model down → fallback provider ya rules-only path, DB slow → cached response. Har mode user-facing message ke saath tested hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Testing strategy batao (project level).'
items.a: Unit tests for pure logic, integration tests for API + DB (containerized), contract tests for schemas, eval regression nightly, aur post-deploy smoke test. CI me gate, aur coverage critical paths par focus.

items.q: Project defense: 'Data privacy kaise handle ki?'
items.a: PII redaction before prompts, logs me masked fields, retention policy short for raw text, aur user delete path (memory + traces). Legal/simple: minimize data, don't log content.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer: production me model badalna ho to kya karoge?'
items.a: Shadow mode me naye model ko production traffic par chalao, offline eval + shadow metrics compare, canary 5% rollout with quality/latency/cost gates, phir full. Rollback ek config change.

items.q: Project defense: 'Aapke project me kaunsi cheez tumhare control me nahi thi?'
items.a: Upstream data quality aur third-party API availability. Isliye schema assertions, retries with backoff, fallback data source, aur degraded mode implement kiya — dependency failure ko predictable banaya.

items.q: Project defense: 'Monitoring se tumhe kaunsa real issue mila?'
items.a: Latency alert ne dikhaya ki ek query ne pool exhaust kiya — fix: index + statement timeout, aur alert actionable ho gaya. Story format: symptom → measurement → fix → verification.

items.q: Project defense: 'Agar 10x data aata to pipeline kaunsa part pehla tootega?'
items.a: Vector index build time aur in-memory aggregation. Plan: incremental/indexed build, sharded retrieval, pre-aggregated tables, aur chunked processing with out-of-core engine (DuckDB/polars).

items.q: Project defense: 'Sabse bada trade-off jo tumne consciously liya?'
items.a: Freshness vs cost: nightly index refresh chuna (realtime embedding costly tha) aur freshness SLA UI me dikhaya ('data as of'). Explicit trade-off + mitigation (on-demand reindex path).

items.q: Project defense: 'Aapne kya automate kiya aur kitna time bacha?'
items.a: Manual data cleanup + weekly report ko scheduled pipeline me convert kiya: 3-4 ghante/week manual work → 2 minute job, aur numbers consistent. Time saved measurable hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer: is project me tumhara contribution kya tha (team project ho to)?'
items.a: Ownership explicitly bolo: 'maine retrieval + eval pipeline banaya, X ne frontend' — aur integration contract kisne define kiya. Team project me ambiguity sabse bura signal hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Kya tum ise dobara banate to kya alag karte?'
items.a: Pehle eval set aur baseline banata (main ne baad me banaya, isliye kuch decisions measurement ke bina liye). Aur logging structured shuru se — debugging time bahut bachta.

items.q: Project defense: 'Aapka system kis problem ko solve karta hai aur kiska nahi?'
items.a: Solves: docs/order/policy ke grounded answers with citations. Doesn't solve: real-time data (freshness lag), open-ended advice, aur high-stakes financial decisions — scope boundaries clearly bolna maturity dikhata hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Security posture kya hai?'
items.a: Auth via JWT with short TTL + refresh, per-tenant data isolation with enforced filters, input validation + size limits, rate limiting, secrets in manager, dependency scanning in CI. Known gap: no WAF, documented.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer: mujhe 3 numbers do jo tumhara kaam prove karte hain.'
items.a: 1) recall@5 0.62 → 0.86 (chunking + hybrid retrieval). 2) p95 latency 1.4s → 400ms (rerank + cache + prompt trim). 3) Cost per task $0.041 → $0.019 (cascade + caching).

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer: dependency failure par system kya karta hai — demo karo.'
items.a: Test se dikha sakta hoon: upstream off karke chalao, response 'degraded' hota hai with retry hint, alert trigger hota hai, aur core flow kaam karta rehta hai.
